title: What happened at that exact moment?
summary: Synchronize commands, gyro motion, PID terms, motors, flight modes, craft attitude, and events on one timeline.
questions: What changed just before the wobble, dip, or disarm?
Did the command, measured response, controller output, or motors move first?
Does the interval support a tuning hypothesis—or only show where to investigate next?

blocks.text: A memorable half-second can look surprisingly polite when averaged across a whole flight. Graph keeps the chronology before an average or score smooths it away: desired rate, measured motion, controller terms, motor commands, mode changes, and craft state can all be read against the same cursor.

steps: Choose Graph and add only the signals needed for the question.
Scrub or play to the event marker or visible disturbance.
Zoom around the interval and use range measurement when duration, oscillation, or spread matters.
Open the Craft section for attitude, motor output, flight mode, and reliable centre-of-gravity context at the shared cursor.
Move to Spectrum when the question becomes frequency behaviour or filter outcome rather than event order.

blocks.caption: A practical tuning-aware signal stack
rows: The desired angular rate presented to the controller—not the aircraft's measured motion.
Whether measured angular rate follows, leads, lags, or departs from the request.
Current-error, accumulated-error, and damping contributions as recorded; availability and exact processing depend on the log and firmware.
Feedforward derived from setpoint change rather than another feedback-error term.
Controller demand and available command headroom; a motor command is not measured thrust.
Whether missing frames or limited logging rate overlap the event under investigation.

blocks.caption: Useful cues, not one-term diagnoses
rows: Limited anticipatory tracking, filter delay, low control authority, or the manoeuvre itself.
Feedforward, filter evidence, motor headroom, and repeated response.
Gyro leads or overshoots near the end of a move
Feedforward timing or an underdamped response.
P:D balance, saturation, mechanics, and comparable moves.
D-term noise, filtering, Feedforward, actuator limits, and physical resonance.
Slow correction or drift after the move
I-Term Relax, anti-windup, saturation, wind, and firmware-specific behaviour.
Noise or oscillation reaching a controller stage.
Spectrum across unfiltered gyro, filtered gyro, D term, and motors.

blocks.title: Order is evidence; cause needs corroboration
blocks.text: No timing pattern maps uniquely to P, I, D, or Feedforward. Filtering, saturation, mechanics, flight input, estimator quality, and several controller terms can create similar traces. Recorded motor output is a command, not proof of motor speed or thrust.

When Graph reveals the right interval, switch to Table without changing the underlying time context. Use the literal samples to challenge the visual story, then use Spectrum or System Response when the question needs frequency or repeated-response evidence.
